Paragraph:
Translation: King Yudhisthira, the son of Kunti, blew his conchshell, the Anantavijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosa and Manipuspaka. That great archer the King of Kasi, the great fighter Sikhandi, Dhrstadyumna, Virata and the unconquerable Satyaki, Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and the others, O King, such as the son of Subhadra, greatly armed, all blew their respective conchshells.

Purport: Sanjaya informed King Dhrtarastra very tactfully that his unwise policy of deceiving the sons of Pandu and endeavoring to enthrone his own sons on the seat of the kingdom was not very laudable. The signs already clearly indicated that the whole Kuru dynasty would be killed in that great battle... The whole catastrophe was due to King Dhrtarastra, because he encouraged the policy followed by his sons.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The rest of the Pandava leadership follows suit, sounding their conchshells in a unified display of strength. Concurrently, the narrator (Sanjaya) uses this overwhelming auditory evidence to confront the blind King Dhrtarastra with the inevitable, disastrous consequences of his deceitful policies.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: The unified blowing of the conchshells solidifies the Pandavas' readiness. Sanjaya tactfully acts as a voice of truth, linking the impending destruction directly to Dhrtarastra's historical enablement of his sons' unrighteous behavior.
Outcome/Resolution: The reality of the impending war is finalized, and accountability for the impending catastrophe is placed squarely on leadership that entertained adharma.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.denial: Willful ignorance, Refusal to see reality
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.guilt: Accountability, Bearing the weight of past actions

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Karma (The inescapable law of cause and effect; the catastrophe is the fruit of deceit)
Adharma (Unrighteousness, which inevitably collapses under the weight of truth)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The text demonstrates the inescapable nature of karma. Dhrtarastra's physical blindness mirrors his spiritual blindness; his enablement of adharma (unrighteousness) has summoned an opposing force of truth that will eradicate his dynasty. Sanjaya serves as the voice of spiritual conscience.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This passage highlights the psychological breaking point of denial. Sanjaya gently but firmly forces Dhrtarastra to confront reality. When individuals or leaders enable toxic behaviors for long periods (like Dhrtarastra did for Duryodhana), the delayed consequences are often catastrophic and unavoidable.
